chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abu Sa'id al-Bajali who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Verily, supplication is more piercing than the spear-head.'

key_terms.أنفذ: More piercing/penetrating — comparative adjective from nufudh (penetration, passage through)
key_terms.الدعاء: Du'a - supplication, earnest prayer and calling upon God
key_terms.السنان: The spear-head, the iron tip of a lance — symbol of military power and lethality

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the power of supplication compared to a spear?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses a vivid military metaphor to convey the exceptional power of du'a (supplication), comparing it to the piercing tip of a spear. This teaching would have resonated deeply with early Muslim audiences who understood the lethal effectiveness of a spear's point; the Imam is saying that du'a cuts through difficulties and reaches its goal with even greater certainty than physical weapons. The statement is placed in a chapter on du'a as the weapon of the believer (momin), emphasizing that the spiritual weapon of prayer is superior to all worldly means.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Abu Saeed Al Bajaly who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The supplication is more piercing than the spear-heads’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from abu Sa’Id al-Bajilli who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Prayer, pleading before Allah for help is more effective than spears.’”
